Real Pi compaction appends a session compaction entry and reloads context from the summary plus kept messages.
Pi auto-compaction triggers near the model limit by default because it uses contextWindow minus reserveTokens, not a 60 percent threshold.
The documented defaults are reserveTokens 16384 and keepRecentTokens 20000, configurable in global or project settings.
Pi extensions can call ctx.getContextUsage() and ctx.compact() from event handlers to trigger actual context compaction.
Pi's trigger-compact extension example checks context usage on turn_end and calls ctx.compact after crossing a token threshold.
Pi exposes session_before_compact and session_compact extension events, allowing custom summary handling and post-compaction observation.
This package already ships Pi extension code through package.json pi.extensions pointing at extensions/cartographer-tools.ts.
Cartographer implementCompact currently produces state resume context by running state-mark-stale, compact-generate, and state-resume, but it does not call Pi ctx.compact.
Prior session evidence showed 12 Cartographer compact-generate calls but only 3 real Pi compaction entries, all near the limit.
A solution can trigger Pi's default compaction instead of replacing the compaction summarizer; custom summaries are optional through session_before_compact.
The published Pi ContextUsage type includes tokens, contextWindow, and percent, so a threshold hook can use percent directly when available.
Pi ctx.compact accepts customInstructions, so Cartographer can focus the default summary without replacing Pi's summarizer.
Cartographer state-resume emits bounded resume context including current phase, next action, working set, known failures, validation refs, and required first response.
